title: Lessons from the ‘Love Lab’ on how to strengthen your relationship, with John Gottman, PhD, and Julie Schwartz Gottman, PhD

sentences.en: Strong, supportive relationships are a key to our mental and even physical health.
sentences.zh: 稳固且相互支持的关系是我们心理健康甚至身体健康的关键。

sentences.en: But what makes for a healthy relationship?
sentences.zh: 但什么样的关系才算健康呢？

sentences.en: Today, we're going to talk about that with two psychologists who spent decades studying the differences between relationship masters and relationship disasters and translating
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将与两位心理学家探讨这个问题。他们花费数十年研究了“关系大师”与“关系灾难”之间的差异，并将

sentences.en: that research into resources for couples and families.
sentences.zh: 这些研究成果转化为夫妻和家庭的实用资源。

sentences.en: So what do relationship masters do that relationship disasters don't?
sentences.zh: 那么，关系大师们做了什么，而关系灾难者们却没有做呢？

sentences.en: What's the right way to fight with your partner?
sentences.zh: 与伴侣争吵的正确方式是什么？

sentences.en: Do fights have to be destructive or is it possible to have a constructive fight?
sentences.zh: 争吵一定是破坏性的吗？还是说有可能进行建设性的争吵？

sentences.en: Is it true that you should never go to bed angry?
sentences.zh: “带着气上床睡觉不好”这种说法是真的吗？

sentences.en: And what are the most important things you can do to make sure your partner feels loved and supported and to strengthen your relationship bond?
sentences.zh: 为了确保伴侣感到被爱和支持，并巩固你们的关系纽带，你能做的最重要的事情是什么？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》（Speaking of Psychology），这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人金·米尔斯（Kim Mills）。

sentences.en: My guests today are Dr. John Gottman and Dr. Julie Schwartz Gottman, the co-founders of the Gottman Institute.
sentences.zh: 今天我的嘉宾是戈特曼研究所（Gottman Institute）的联合创始人约翰·戈特曼博士（Dr. John Gottman）和朱莉·施瓦茨·戈特曼博士（Dr. Julie Schwartz Gottman）。

sentences.en: Dr. John Gottman began his research on marital stability and divorce prediction in the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 约翰·戈特曼博士在20世纪70年代开始了他关于婚姻稳定性和离婚预测的研究。

sentences.en: He's an emeritus professor of psychology at the University of Washington, where he founded the Love Lab and where much of his research on couples interactions was conducted.
sentences.zh: 他是华盛顿大学的心理学荣誉退休教授，在那里他创立了“爱情实验室”（Love Lab），并进行了大量关于夫妻互动的研究。

sentences.en: Dr. Gottman is the author or co-author of more than 200 academic articles and has won numerous awards for his research.
sentences.zh: 戈特曼博士是200多篇学术文章的作者或合著者，并因其研究获得了无数奖项。

sentences.en: Dr. Julie Schwartz Gottman is a clinical psychologist with expertise working with distressed couples,
sentences.zh: 朱莉·施瓦茨·戈特曼博士是一位临床心理学家，擅长处理陷入困境的夫妻关系，

sentences.en: abuse and trauma survivors, and people with substance use problems and their partners.
sentences.zh: 以及虐待和创伤幸存者、有药物滥用问题的人及其伴侣的心理咨询。

sentences.en: She brings her expertise in clinical psychology to the Gottman Institute, co-creating the Art
sentences.zh: 她将自己在临床心理学方面的专业知识带到了戈特曼研究所，共同创建了“爱情的艺术与科学”

sentences.en: and Science of Love workshops for couples, and co-designing the National Clinical Training Program in Gottman Method Couples Therapy.
sentences.zh: 夫妻工作坊，并共同设计了戈特曼方法夫妻治疗的国家临床培训项目。

sentences.en: Together, the Gottmans have translated the science of relationships into books, workshops, trainings for therapists, and other resources for the public.
sentences.zh: 戈特曼夫妇共同将关系科学转化为书籍、工作坊、治疗师培训以及其他面向公众的资源。

sentences.en: They've co-authored many books together, including their latest, Fight Right, How to Turn
sentences.zh: 他们合著了许多书籍，包括他们最新的作品《正确争吵：如何将冲突转化为联结》（Fight Right, How to Turn

sentences.en: Conflict into Connection.
sentences.zh: 化冲突为联结。

sentences.en: They've also practiced what they preach in their own nearly four-decade marriage.
sentences.zh: 在他们自己近四十年的婚姻中，他们也践行着自己所倡导的理念。

sentences.en: Dr. Gottman, Dr. Schwartz Gottman, thank you both for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 戈特曼博士、施瓦茨·戈特曼博士，非常感谢二位今天能来参加节目。

sentences.en: Thank you, Kim.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，金。

sentences.en: Thank you, Kim.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，金。

sentences.en: We're really happy to be here.
sentences.zh: 我们很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: Let's start by talking about the background each of you brings to this work.
sentences.zh: 让我们先从你们各自从事这项工作的背景谈起吧。

sentences.en: John, you're a researcher, and Julie, you've always been a practicing clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 约翰，你是一位研究员；朱莉，你一直是一位执业临床心理学家。

sentences.en: How did you decide to bring your work together into what became the Gottman Institute?
sentences.zh: 你们是如何决定将各自的工作结合起来，并最终成立戈特曼研究所的呢？

sentences.en: Well, here's how it happened.
sentences.zh: 嗯，事情是这样的。

sentences.en: John and I met in 1986, married in 87.
sentences.zh: 我和约翰在1986年相识，1987年结婚。

sentences.en: I, at the time, was working with very severe trauma, as well as some of the other fields you mentioned, Kim.
sentences.zh: 当时，我正在处理非常严重的创伤案例，以及你提到的其他一些领域的问题，金。

sentences.en: But every night at dinner, I was listening to John talk about his research, and I got sucked in.
sentences.zh: 但每天晚餐时，我都会听约翰谈论他的研究，我被深深吸引了。

sentences.en: I was desperately trying to be individuated, which was popular at the time, but it didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 我当时拼命想保持独立，这在当时很流行，但没能实现。

sentences.en: We merged completely.
sentences.zh: 我们完全融合在了一起。

sentences.en: And now, four decades later, I have half a brain, he has half a brain, but together we make one brain.
sentences.zh: 四十年后的今天，我有一半大脑，他有一半大脑，但我们合在一起就是一个完整的大脑。

sentences.en: So, basically, we were out in a canoe about six, seven years later, and I said, honey, why
sentences.zh: 所以，基本上，大约六七年后，我们划着独木舟出去玩，我对他说，亲爱的，为什么

sentences.en: don't we take this work out of the ivory tower and into the population who desperately needs help?
sentences.zh: 我们不把这些研究成果从象牙塔里带出来，带给那些急需帮助的普通大众呢？

sentences.en: We've learned a lot from your research, and there's no point in leaving it in the university.
sentences.zh: 我们从你的研究中学到了很多，把它们留在大学里毫无意义。

sentences.en: Let's take it out and bring it to the people.
sentences.zh: 让我们把它带出来，带给人们。

sentences.en: And that's what we did.
sentences.zh: 于是我们就这么做了。

sentences.en: So, John, one of the most well-known findings of your early research was that you were able to predict whether a couple would divorce years later just by analyzing a few minutes
sentences.zh: 那么，约翰，你早期研究中最著名的发现之一是，你仅通过分析几分钟的视频，就能预测一对夫妻多年后是否会离婚，

sentences.en: of video of their interactions early in their marriage.
sentences.zh: 而这些视频记录的是他们婚姻早期的互动。

sentences.en: Tell us about that work.
sentences.zh: 能跟我们讲讲那项工作吗？

sentences.en: How did you do that research?
sentences.zh: 你是如何进行那项研究的？

sentences.en: And what clues to a relationship's outcome were evidenced so early on?
sentences.zh: 在关系早期，有哪些迹象预示了最终的结果？

sentences.en: Well, this research was really done in conjunction with my best friend, Robert Levinson, who is a psychology professor at UC Berkeley.
sentences.zh: 这项研究实际上是我和我最好的朋友、加州大学伯克利分校的心理学教授罗伯特·莱文森（Robert Levinson）共同完成的。

sentences.en: And Bob and I had a lab back in the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 鲍勃（Bob）和我在20世纪70年代拥有一个实验室。

sentences.en: We had our own computer, which was very unusual in the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 我们有自己的电脑，这在70年代非常罕见。

sentences.en: Every university had one big mainframe computer.
sentences.zh: 当时每所大学只有一台大型主机电脑。

sentences.en: But Bob and I had a computer called a PDP-11, which is about the size of three refrigerators.
sentences.zh: 但鲍勃和我有一台PDP-11电脑，大约有三个冰箱那么大。

sentences.en: And all it did was synchronize the video time code to physiological measures we're collecting from both people as they talk to each other.
sentences.zh: 它唯一的功能就是将视频时间码与我们在两人交谈时收集的生理指标同步。

sentences.en: We're measuring respiration, heart rate, blood velocity, skin conductance, how much they jiggled and moved.
sentences.zh: 我们测量呼吸、心率、血流速度、皮肤电导，以及他们身体晃动和移动的幅度。

sentences.en: And so we had couples meet at the end of the day after being apart for at least eight hours.
sentences.zh: 我们让夫妻在分开至少八小时后，在一天结束时见面。

sentences.en: And once we got good physiological signals, we just asked them to talk about how their day went and videotape that.
sentences.zh: 一旦我们获得了良好的生理信号，就让他们谈谈这一天过得怎么样，并录下视频。

sentences.en: And then we interviewed them about the major conflict areas in their relationship and had them pick the top area to talk about for 15 minutes.
sentences.zh: 然后我们采访他们关于关系中主要的冲突领域，并让他们挑选出最核心的问题讨论15分钟。

sentences.en: And we asked them to try to solve the problem.
sentences.zh: 我们要求他们尝试解决这个问题。

sentences.en: And then they selected from a list of positive topics like planning a vacation, talk for another
sentences.zh: 之后，他们从一份积极话题清单中选择一个，比如计划度假，再谈论

sentences.en: 15 minutes.
sentences.zh: 15分钟。

sentences.en: When they were done with that, they separately viewed their videotapes and were still collecting
sentences.zh: 当他们完成这些后，他们会分别观看自己的录像，而我们仍在收集

sentences.en: physiological data and videotape as they watched their tapes and turned a dial to let
sentences.zh: 生理数据和录像。当他们观看录像时，会转动一个拨盘来告诉

sentences.en: us know inside what they were feeling from the dial to range from very negative to very positive.
sentences.zh: 我们他们内心的感受，拨盘的范围从非常负面到非常正面。

sentences.en: And then we basically sent them home.
sentences.zh: 然后我们基本上就让他们回家了。

sentences.en: Bob and I had no clue of how to help anybody at that time.
sentences.zh: 当时鲍勃和我根本不知道如何帮助任何人。

sentences.en: And our own intuitions were terrible because we were going from one disastrous relationship with a woman to another.
sentences.zh: 我们自己的直觉也很糟糕，因为我们当时正从一段糟糕的关系跳到另一段糟糕的关系中。

sentences.en: And our ignorances really motivated this research because we had no hypotheses at all.
sentences.zh: 我们的无知确实促成了这项研究，因为我们当时没有任何假设。

sentences.en: Well, three years later, we recontacted these couples and it turned out that we could predict
sentences.zh: 三年后，我们重新联系了这些夫妻，结果发现我们可以

sentences.en: with over 90% accuracy how the relationship had changed over that three-year period, whether couples got happier or less happy, whether they broke up or not.
sentences.zh: 以超过90%的准确率预测这三年间关系的变化，比如夫妻是变得更幸福还是更不幸福，是否分手了等等。

sentences.en: So the predictions were very high and that was very unusual at that time for psychologists to have that level of prediction.
sentences.zh: 所以预测准确率非常高，这在当时对心理学家来说是非常罕见的。

sentences.en: And it turned out that just about everywhere we looked, we could tell the difference between
sentences.zh: 结果发现，几乎在我们观察的每一个方面，我们都能区分出

sentences.en: the people who were in disastrous relationships like the ones Bob and I had and the people who were really masters of relationship.
sentences.zh: 那些处于糟糕关系中的人（就像鲍勃和我当时那样）和那些真正掌握了关系经营之道的大师。

sentences.en: And even when they talked about how their day went, the disasters went out of their way
sentences.zh: 即使在谈论他们一天过得如何时，那些关系糟糕的人也会特意

sentences.en: to communicate their boredom and lack of interest in their partner's day, whereas the masters
sentences.zh: 表现出厌倦和对伴侣的一天缺乏兴趣，而关系大师们

sentences.en: were totally involved and interested, asked a lot of questions and communicated that they really cared about how their partner's day went.
sentences.zh: 则完全投入并表现出兴趣，会问很多问题，并传达出他们真的很关心伴侣这一天过得如何。

sentences.en: During conflict, we had our best prediction of the future of a relationship.
sentences.zh: 在冲突期间，我们对关系未来的预测最为准确。

sentences.en: And it turned out there that when we look just as simply at the ratio, the number of seconds
sentences.zh: 结果发现，当我们简单地观察比例时，即人们对彼此友好的秒数

sentences.en: that people were nice to one another divided by the number of seconds that they were nasty to one another, that ratio averaged five to one among the masters and averaged 0.8 among
sentences.zh: 除以他们对彼此恶劣的秒数，这个比例在关系大师中平均为5比1，而在

sentences.en: the disasters, a little bit more negativity.
sentences.zh: 关系灾难者中平均为0.8，负面情绪更多一些。

sentences.en: And in particular, there were four things that couples did in relationships that were doomed that really predicted the future very well.
sentences.zh: 特别是有四种行为，在注定失败的关系中，这些行为能很好地预测未来。

sentences.en: They started with criticism.
sentences.zh: 他们以批评开始。

sentences.en: They used contempt.
sentences.zh: 他们使用蔑视。

sentences.en: They were defensive.
sentences.zh: 他们表现出防御性。

sentences.en: And when they got physiologically aroused, when their heart rates exceeded 100 beats a minute, they would withdraw from the interaction and stonewall and not give any cues to the
sentences.zh: 当他们生理上感到激动，心率超过每分钟100次时，他们会从互动中撤退，筑起高墙（stonewall），不给

sentences.en: speaker that they were listening and interested.
sentences.zh: 说话者任何他们正在倾听或感兴趣的暗示。

sentences.en: So those behaviors we wound up calling the four horsemen of the apocalypse.
sentences.zh: 所以我们最终将这些行为称为“末日四骑士”。

sentences.en: But I must say that Bob and I had no clue of how to help anybody.
sentences.zh: 但我必须说，鲍勃和我当时根本不知道如何帮助任何人。

sentences.en: And without Julie's clinical experience, we never would have figured out how to help people.
sentences.zh: 如果没有朱莉的临床经验，我们永远也无法找出帮助人们的方法。

sentences.en: We needed the researcher and the therapist to really combine their knowledge.
sentences.zh: 我们需要研究人员和治疗师真正结合他们的知识。

sentences.en: And Julie's knowledge of how to help extremely distressed people was essential in building a therapy for helping people.
sentences.zh: 朱莉在帮助极度痛苦的人方面的知识，对于建立一套帮助人们的治疗方法至关重要。

sentences.en: But then that material, your research data must have been sitting there for a while, right, before you met Julie.
sentences.zh: 但是，那些材料，你的研究数据一定在那儿放了一段时间，对吧，在你遇到朱莉之前。

sentences.en: I mean, Julie, when did you come on the scene and start looking at all of this and then coming up with your part of the whole theory?
sentences.zh: 我是说，朱莉，你是什么时候出现在现场，开始审视所有这些，并提出你那部分理论的呢？

sentences.en: We started working together.
sentences.zh: 我们开始一起工作。

sentences.en: So, of course, I was hearing it every night at dinner, beginning in 1987.
sentences.zh: 当然，从1987年开始，我每天晚餐时都在听这些内容。

sentences.en: But then in 19, about 92, maybe 93, we started really trying to analyze theoretically what the successful couples were doing to create the success of their relationships.
sentences.zh: 但在1992年或93年左右，我们开始真正尝试从理论上分析成功的夫妻在做什么，从而创造了他们关系的成功。

sentences.en: So we were already, John had analyzed the data.
sentences.zh: 所以我们当时已经在做了，约翰已经分析了数据。

sentences.en: He discovered the four horsemen of the apocalypse.
sentences.zh: 他发现了“末日四骑士”。

sentences.en: There were also really important factors involving supporting friendships and also what created shared
sentences.zh: 还有一些非常重要的因素，涉及支持性的友谊，以及是什么为夫妻创造了共享的

sentences.en: meaning for the couple, which meant not only talking about what values they shared, but
sentences.zh: 意义，这意味着不仅要谈论他们共享的价值观，还要谈论

sentences.en: what each individual partner valued deeply and really communicating that with their partner and each partner supporting the other person's dreams and values.
sentences.zh: 每个伴侣内心深处珍视的东西，并真正与伴侣沟通，每个伴侣都要支持对方的梦想和价值观。

sentences.en: So we began to create our theory, which we called the sound relationship house theory.
sentences.zh: 所以我们开始建立我们的理论，我们称之为“幸福关系屋理论”（Sound Relationship House Theory）。

sentences.en: And later on, the brilliant John Gottman began to do much more mathematical analyses back in
sentences.zh: 后来，天才的约翰·戈特曼在1990年左右开始进行更多的数学分析，

sentences.en: about 1990 and began to discover what we called the trust metric, which was a mathematical formulation
sentences.zh: 并开始发现我们所说的“信任指标”（trust metric），这是一个数学公式，

sentences.en: that really predicted whether couples retained trust or had lost it, as well as looking at commitment in the couple.
sentences.zh: 它能真正预测夫妻是保持了信任还是失去了信任，同时也观察夫妻间的承诺度。

sentences.en: Then we looked at what did the successful couples do and combining our knowledge, our information
sentences.zh: 然后我们观察成功的夫妻做了什么，结合我们的知识和信息

sentences.en: base, we created interventions that helped couples do what the successful couples did.
sentences.zh: 库，我们创建了干预措施，帮助夫妻去做那些成功夫妻所做的事情。

sentences.en: Now, mind you, nobody took relationships one-on-one in high school or college.
sentences.zh: 要知道，在高中或大学里，没有人教过我们如何处理一对一的关系。

sentences.en: You know, we still don't, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们现在仍然没有教，对吧？

sentences.en: So people really were at loss.
sentences.zh: 所以人们真的感到很迷茫。

sentences.en: They were groping in the dark for what the heck do we do instead of the bad patterns and behaviors we're using with one another.
sentences.zh: 他们像在黑暗中摸索，不知道除了我们彼此之间使用的那些糟糕模式和行为外，还能做什么。

sentences.en: So John wrote his first popular book.
sentences.zh: 所以约翰写了他的第一本大众书籍。

sentences.en: When was that, honey?
sentences.zh: 那是什么时候，亲爱的？

sentences.en: Right around 1990 something, 1999.
sentences.zh: 大约在1990几年，1999年左右。

sentences.en: And lo and behold, people grabbed hold of it and really, really were hungry for more.
sentences.zh: 结果人们争相阅读，真的非常渴望了解更多。

sentences.en: So we worked on interventions.
sentences.zh: 所以我们致力于干预措施。

sentences.en: We created a couple's workshop, a two-day workshop that we later tested that created a huge difference
sentences.zh: 我们创建了一个夫妻工作坊，一个为期两天的研讨会，后来我们测试发现，它产生了巨大的差异，

sentences.en: in not only sustaining friendship or creating friendship in partners, but really helping them
sentences.zh: 不仅在维持友谊或在伴侣间建立友谊方面，而且真正帮助他们

sentences.en: to manage conflict in, as you said earlier, Kim, a constructive way rather than a destructive
sentences.zh: 以一种建设性的方式，正如你之前所说，金，来管理冲突，而不是以破坏性的

sentences.en: way, replacing the four horseman with much more listening, much better description of I, I feel,
sentences.zh: 方式，用更多的倾听、更好的“我”的描述来取代四骑士，比如“我感到”、“我正在思考”、“我正在想象”、“我正在幻想”，而不是指责和责怪伴侣。

sentences.en: So when you averaged it all out, it looked like there was no change, but actually the rich got richer and the poor got poorer in the sense of the relationships.
sentences.zh: 所以当你把所有这些平均起来时，看起来好像没有什么变化，但实际上富者更富，贫者更贫，就人际关系而言。

sentences.en: Let's talk for a few minutes about your most recent book, Fight Right, How to Turn Conflict into
sentences.zh: 让我们花几分钟谈谈你们最近的书，《正确争吵：如何将冲突转化为

sentences.en: Connection.
sentences.zh: 连接》。

sentences.en: What does it mean to fight right?
sentences.zh: 正确争吵意味着什么？

sentences.en: So fighting right means in a nutshell, fighting to understand, fighting to understand.
sentences.zh: 所以正确争吵简而言之，意味着为了理解而争吵，为了理解而争吵。

sentences.en: So, you know, even as a therapist sitting across from a client I've known for a year, let's say, I never assume I really understand anything fully unless I ask more
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，即使作为一名治疗师，坐在我认识了一年的客户对面，假设我永远不会认为我完全理解任何事情，除非我问更多

sentences.en: questions, I really listen much more carefully and so on.
sentences.zh: 问题，我真的很仔细地倾听等等。

sentences.en: And the questions need to be the deepening questions, not questions that remain superficial.
sentences.zh: 而且问题需要是深层的问题，而不是停留在表面的问题。

sentences.en: So fighting right really means, first of all, trying to eliminate as many of the four horsemen as we can.
sentences.zh: 所以正确争吵确实意味着，首先，尽量消除我们能消除的尽可能多的“天启四骑士”。

sentences.en: You know, nobody's perfect here and we're not going for the perfect relationship.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这里没有人是完美的，我们追求的不是完美的关系。

sentences.en: You know, I'm always going to sink back into some criticism every now and then and defensiveness.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我总是会时不时地陷入一些批评和防御之中。

sentences.en: And my darling partner may as well, though we really try hard to avoid as much as we can.
sentences.zh: 我亲爱的伴侣也可能如此，尽管我们确实非常努力地尽可能避免。

sentences.en: So what takes the place of those, right?
sentences.zh: 那么什么取代了这些呢，对吧？

sentences.en: This book really focuses in on how to make calm, constructive, and more compassionate our conflict conversations, rather than those escalations that many of us have experienced.
sentences.zh: 这本书确实专注于如何让我们的冲突对话变得冷静、建设性和更具同情心，而不是我们许多人经历过的那种升级。

sentences.en: Those times when we get flooded, meaning we go into fight or flight when we're so upset that our physiology is jacking up and our heart rates are over 100 beats a minute,
sentences.zh: 那些我们被淹没的时候，意味着当我们如此心烦意乱以至于生理机能激增，心率超过每分钟100次时，我们就会进入战斗或逃跑状态，

sentences.en: we can't think straight, we can't listen well, we can't creatively problem solve at all.
sentences.zh: 我们无法清晰思考，无法很好地倾听，根本无法创造性地解决问题。

sentences.en: Our prefrontal cortex is offline.
sentences.zh: 我们的前额叶皮层离线了。

sentences.en: So this book gives very specific practical information about how to create fights as a pathway to understanding.
sentences.zh: 所以这本书提供了关于如何创造争吵作为通往理解之路的具体实用信息。

sentences.en: That doesn't mean you should, you know, seek out lots of fighting.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着你应该，你知道，寻求大量的争吵。

sentences.en: There's many ways of understanding one another, but fights happen.
sentences.zh: 有很多互相理解的方式，但争吵会发生。

sentences.en: They happen to almost everyone.
sentences.zh: 它们几乎发生在每个人身上。

sentences.en: And at the time that we started writing this book, the country was incredibly polarized.
sentences.zh: 在我们开始写这本书的时候，这个国家极度两极分化。

sentences.en: It is still today, as all of us know.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所有人所知，今天仍然如此。

sentences.en: And, you know, we were, you know, very astounded at how little listening was happening between folks in
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们，你知道，对在一个阵营的人与

sentences.en: one compartment versus folks in another, who had very different ideas about the way things should be.
sentences.zh: 另一个阵营的人之间发生的倾听是多么少感到非常震惊，他们对事情应该是什么样子有非常不同的想法。

sentences.en: So we thought, well, my God, you know, we're never going to stop fighting.
sentences.zh: 所以我们想，好吧，天哪，你知道，我们永远不会停止争吵。

sentences.en: But we have to help folks, if we can, learn how to fight so that there's greater understanding, even if there's still disagreement.
sentences.zh: 但如果可以的话，我们必须帮助人们学习如何争吵，以便有更好的理解，即使仍然存在分歧。

sentences.en: And that is what this book provides.
sentences.zh: 而这就是这本书所提供的。

sentences.en: So what are the common types of fights and how should couples handle?
sentences.zh: 那么常见的争吵类型有哪些，夫妻应该如何处理？

sentences.en: Here's the interesting thing.
sentences.zh: 有趣的事情在这里。

sentences.en: Most couples fight about absolutely nothing.
sentences.zh: 大多数夫妻争吵的都是完全无关紧要的事情。

sentences.en: Fights emerge out of these moments of disconnection and where people are left alone.
sentences.zh: 争吵源于这些脱节的时刻，人们被独自留下。

sentences.en: When they're reaching out for something, their partner, and it doesn't go right.
sentences.zh: 当他们向某人，他们的伴侣寻求什么，却进展不顺利时。

sentences.en: Like they're watching TV together and they've made popcorn and he's got the remote and she says, leave it at that station.
sentences.zh: 就像他们一起看电视，爆米花做好了，他拿着遥控器，她说，停在那个频道。

sentences.en: He says, well, yeah, let me see what else is on.
sentences.zh: 他说，好吧，是的，让我看看还有什么。

sentences.en: She says, no, leave it.
sentences.zh: 她说，不，停在那。

sentences.en: He says, well, let me see what else is on.
sentences.zh: 他说，好吧，让我看看还有什么。

sentences.en: She says, I said, leave it.
sentences.zh: 她说，我说，停在那。

sentences.en: And he says, you know, I don't even want to talk to you.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，我甚至不想和你说话。

sentences.en: You know, and he throws the remote down.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他把遥控器扔了下去。

sentences.en: What are they fighting about?
sentences.zh: 他们在争吵什么？

sentences.en: Now they're not fighting about in-laws, money, sex, they're fighting about the lack of connection.
sentences.zh: 现在他们不是在争吵姻亲、金钱、性，他们是在争吵缺乏连接。

sentences.en: And that is the thing that
sentences.zh: 而这就是

sentences.en: Julie was emphasizing.
sentences.zh: 朱莉一直在强调的事情。

sentences.en: Conflict always has a goal, which is mutual understanding.
sentences.zh: 冲突总有一个目标，那就是相互理解。

sentences.en: We actually need conflict to continue to love each other over time as we both change.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上需要冲突，以便随着我们两个人的变化，在未来继续相爱。

sentences.en: And so really what we're doing in the book, Fight Right, is helping people understand these situations where they're actually
sentences.zh: 所以我们在这本书《正确争吵》中真正做的是，帮助人们理解这些情况，在这些情况下，他们实际上

sentences.en: reaching out for one another for emotional connection most of the time and being left alone.
sentences.zh: 大部分时间都在向对方寻求情感连接，却被独自留下。

sentences.en: Let me jump in and add a little bit more here.
sentences.zh: 让我插一句，再补充一点。

sentences.en: In some of John's earliest research, and we find this still to be true, there are three types of conflicts management styles that people may have.
sentences.zh: 在约翰最早的一些研究中，我们发现这仍然是事实，人们可能有三种类型的冲突管理风格。

sentences.en: One is what we call avoiders, conflict avoiders.
sentences.zh: 一种是我们所说的回避者，冲突回避者。

sentences.en: And those are folks who, you know, of course, they're going to have disagreements, they're going to have differences, oftentimes based
sentences.zh: 这些人，你知道，当然，他们会有分歧，他们会有差异，通常基于

sentences.en: in lifestyle preferences or personality differences.
sentences.zh: 生活方式偏好或个性差异。

sentences.en: But what they do, they may express just a little bit of what they think or what they feel.
sentences.zh: 但他们所做的，他们可能只会表达一点点他们的想法或感受。

sentences.en: But then they say, okay, not a big deal.
sentences.zh: 但随后他们会说，好吧，没什么大不了的。

sentences.en: You know, let's drop it.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，咱们别提这事了。

sentences.en: Let's just agree to disagree.
sentences.zh: 我们还是保留各自的意见吧。

sentences.en: And they go on with their lives.
sentences.zh: 然后他们继续过自己的生活。

sentences.en: Those are conflict avoiders.
sentences.zh: 那些是回避冲突型的人。

sentences.en: Then we have conflict validators.
sentences.zh: 接下来是验证型的人。

sentences.en: And validators are folks who stay fairly calm and fairly rational.
sentences.zh: 验证型的人通常比较冷静，也比较理性。

sentences.en: However, they do express their feelings about a particular issue, but they'll do so quickly.
sentences.zh: 不过，他们确实会表达对某个特定问题的感受，但他们会很快表达出来。

sentences.en: And then they'll move into problem solving, you know, very fast and they work on problem solving.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会非常迅速地进入解决问题的阶段，并致力于解决问题。

sentences.en: So those are validators.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是验证型的人。

sentences.en: And then we have the volatiles of which I am a proud member.
sentences.zh: 接下来是波动型的人，我很自豪自己就是其中一员。

sentences.en: And volatiles are folks who express their feelings passionately, intensely.
sentences.zh: 波动型的人表达感受时充满激情，非常强烈。

sentences.en: They immediately jump to 60 miles an hour and they express feelings intensely.
sentences.zh: 他们会立刻进入高亢状态，强烈地表达自己的感受。

sentences.en: That doesn't mean that they're flooded.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着他们情绪失控了。

sentences.en: There's a real difference between being physiologically flooded and expressing things passionately and intensely.
sentences.zh: 生理上的情绪过载与充满激情、强烈地表达感受之间有着本质的区别。

sentences.en: One doesn't necessarily go with the other.
sentences.zh: 前者并不一定伴随着后者。

sentences.en: So volatiles will express feelings very, very intensely.
sentences.zh: 所以，波动型的人会非常、非常强烈地表达感受。

sentences.en: And eventually they'll get into working on compromise.
sentences.zh: 最终他们也会开始寻求妥协。

sentences.en: But all that passionate feeling comes out firSt. So those are our conflict volatiles.
sentences.zh: 但所有那些激情的感受会先宣泄出来。这就是我们的冲突波动型。

sentences.en: And people typically are mismatched.
sentences.zh: 人们通常在类型上是不匹配的。

sentences.en: So in our relationship, for example, John is a wonderful conflict avoider or maybe a little bit of a validator.
sentences.zh: 比如在我们的关系中，约翰是一个很棒的冲突回避型，或者稍微带点验证型。

sentences.en: And I'm a delightful volatile.
sentences.zh: 而我是一个可爱的波动型。

sentences.en: Now he can also be in his best moments, I should say.
sentences.zh: 当然，他也有表现最好的时候，我得这么说。

sentences.en: And then we're off and running.
sentences.zh: 然后我们就开始行动了。

sentences.en: So, you know, we have to talk sometimes about the differences in our style of how we want to talk about a conflict, how we want
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们有时必须讨论一下我们处理冲突风格上的差异，我们想如何

sentences.en: to process trying to just understand one another's position on an issue, given, let's say, that one just doesn't want to talk about it at all.
sentences.zh: 处理那些试图理解对方立场的问题，假设其中一方根本不想谈论它。

sentences.en: There's our avoider.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们的回避型。

sentences.en: And one passionately wants to talk about it.
sentences.zh: 而另一方却迫切地想谈论它。

sentences.en: There's our volatile.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们的波动型。

sentences.en: How are they going to arrive at a system in which they can talk gently with one another without the volatile scaring away the avoider and the avoider angering the volatile?
sentences.zh: 他们该如何建立一种沟通机制，既能温和地交流，又不至于让波动型吓跑回避型，或者让回避型激怒波动型呢？

sentences.en: So that's a conversation in itself that is an important one to have when there is an extreme difference.
sentences.zh: 所以，当双方存在极大差异时，这本身就是一个非常重要的对话。

sentences.en: But couples work that stuff out all the time.
sentences.zh: 但夫妻们一直在解决这些问题。

sentences.en: So and all three types of couples can have successful relationships.
sentences.zh: 所以，这三种类型的夫妻都能拥有成功的关系。

sentences.en: All of them, as long as they have that five to one, as long as that's it, as long
sentences.zh: 所有这些类型，只要他们能保持五比一的比例，只要能做到这一点，只要

sentences.en: as they have that five to one ratio of positive to negative interactions that they're having during the conflict itself.
sentences.zh: 他们在冲突本身的过程中保持五比一的积极与消极互动比例。

sentences.en: So I want to go back to the couple who are having the argument over the remote.
sentences.zh: 我想回到那对为了遥控器争吵的夫妻身上。

sentences.en: So what is the solution?
sentences.zh: 那么解决方案是什么呢？

sentences.en: I mean, how should you work that out in a way that doesn't, I mean, should the woman go to another room and watch a different TV or how do you resolve that?
sentences.zh: 我是说，该如何解决这个问题才不会……我是说，妻子应该去另一个房间看不同的电视吗？或者你该如何解决这个问题？

sentences.en: Well, part of it is really understanding what's underneath that unhappiness around the remote and understanding that there's a power struggle there.
sentences.zh: 嗯，部分原因在于真正理解遥控器背后那种不快乐的根源，并意识到其中存在权力斗争。

sentences.en: And maybe there's a power struggle in their relationship in general.
sentences.zh: 也许他们的关系中普遍存在权力斗争。

sentences.en: And it feels unfair to one or both people.
sentences.zh: 这对其中一方或双方来说都感到不公平。

sentences.en: And that sort of gets underneath the issue of the remote.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上触及了遥控器问题的本质。

sentences.en: The remote is kind of a surface issue of this perceived inequity and power in the relationship.
sentences.zh: 遥控器只是这种关系中感知到的不平等和权力问题的表面现象。

sentences.en: So by asking those six questions that Julie mentioned earlier, they wind up really looking at the dreams within the conflict.
sentences.zh: 所以，通过问朱莉之前提到的那六个问题，他们最终真正审视了冲突背后的梦想。

sentences.en: And once those get surfaced, there's much more empathy and understanding.
sentences.zh: 一旦这些梦想浮出水面，就会有更多的同理心和理解。

sentences.en: And they get to this, the real goal of conflict, which is mutual understanding.
sentences.zh: 他们就能达到冲突的真正目标，即相互理解。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, I think there's another part of this too, which is accepting influence.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为这还有另一个层面，那就是接受影响力。

sentences.en: We found that it was incredibly important for people to accept influence from the other person.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，人们接受对方的影响力是非常重要的。

sentences.en: And in particular, in heterosexual relationships, not surprisingly, given social conditioning in our culture, it was more
sentences.zh: 特别是在异性恋关系中，不出所料，考虑到我们文化中的社会习俗，

sentences.en: important for men to accept influence from their female partners, typically then vice versa.
sentences.zh: 男性接受女性伴侣的影响力通常比反过来更重要。

sentences.en: So accepting influence means, okay, honey, I'll let you stay on this channel.
sentences.zh: 所以，接受影响力意味着，好吧，亲爱的，我让你看这个频道。

sentences.en: Let's stay on this channel and we'll see if we both like it.
sentences.zh: 我们就看这个频道，看看我们俩是否都喜欢。

sentences.en: And then maybe, you know, we can look around a little bit more.
sentences.zh: 然后也许，你知道，我们可以再看看别的。

sentences.en: How does that sound?
sentences.zh: 你觉得怎么样？

sentences.en: So you just brought up sexual orientation, just the idea of same-sex couples, opposite-sex couples.
sentences.zh: 你刚才提到了性取向，也就是同性伴侣和异性伴侣的概念。

sentences.en: Do the patterns that you have observed, do they hold true for both?
sentences.zh: 你们观察到的模式，对两者都适用吗？

sentences.en: Or because of socialization, will you find same-sex couples will behave differently because two women together, they were socialized the same way.
sentences.zh: 还是说由于社会化过程，你会发现同性伴侣的行为会有所不同，因为两个女性在一起，她们受到的社会化教育是一样的。

sentences.en: Two men together, they were socialized the same way.
sentences.zh: 两个男性在一起，他们受到的社会化教育也是一样的。

sentences.en: What happens?
sentences.zh: 会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Bob and I were quite surprised when we studied gay and lesbian relationships for a dozen years that, in fact,
sentences.zh: 所以，当我和鲍勃研究同性恋关系长达十二年时，我们感到非常惊讶，事实上，

sentences.en: gay and lesbian couples are a lot nicer to each other than heterosexual couples.
sentences.zh: 同性恋伴侣比异性恋伴侣对彼此要友好得多。

sentences.en: They have more of a sense of humor about themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们对自己更有幽默感。

sentences.en: They're gentler in the way they present an issue.
sentences.zh: 他们在提出问题时更温和。

sentences.en: They can laugh at themselves more easily.
sentences.zh: 他们更容易自嘲。

sentences.en: And they're much more direct when it comes to their needs about sexual intimacy than heterosexual couples.
sentences.zh: 而且在涉及性亲密需求时，他们比异性恋伴侣要直接得多。

sentences.en: So, you know, we were pretty surprised by that.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们对此感到非常惊讶。

sentences.en: And it turns out that that's really kind of a general finding that we heterosexual couples have a lot to learn.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这确实是一个普遍的发现，我们异性恋伴侣有很多东西需要学习。

sentences.en: John, does the advice that you've developed for couples work for other relationships, for example, parents and children, other family relationships, friendships?
sentences.zh: 约翰，你为夫妻制定的建议是否适用于其他关系，例如父母与子女、其他家庭关系、友谊？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: One of the things that I was very interested in, Bob wasn't too interested in
sentences.zh: 我非常感兴趣的一件事是，鲍勃对

sentences.en: parent-child interaction, but I was very interested in children and their development and to investigate
sentences.zh: 亲子互动不太感兴趣，但我对儿童及其发展非常感兴趣，并调查了

sentences.en: how parent relationships affected children and how children affected the parental relationships.
sentences.zh: 父母关系如何影响孩子，以及孩子如何影响父母关系。

sentences.en: We did some longitudinal research and looked at parent-child interaction, and we discovered an amazing thing that there were some parents who really were emotion coaches
sentences.zh: 我们做了一些纵向研究，观察了亲子互动，我们发现了一件惊人的事情，有些父母确实是孩子的情绪教练

sentences.en: of their children.
sentences.zh: 他们的孩子。

sentences.en: They really took these moments when their children were feeling strongly about something, feeling heard or rejected.
sentences.zh: 当孩子对某事有强烈感受时，感到被倾听或被拒绝时，他们真的抓住了这些时刻。

sentences.en: And some parents would try to minimize that and cheer their child up and help their child get over the moment.
sentences.zh: 有些父母会试图淡化这种情绪，哄孩子开心，帮助孩子度过那一刻。

sentences.en: And other parents would really focus in on that moment and see it as an opportunity for learning or teaching or getting closer to their child.
sentences.zh: 而另一些父母则会真正专注于那一刻，将其视为学习、教导或与孩子拉近距离的机会。

sentences.en: And they would do five things as emotion coaches, you know, help their child understand the emotions,
sentences.zh: 作为情绪教练，他们会做五件事，你知道，帮助孩子理解情绪，

sentences.en: put labels on those feelings, help their child problem solve if they were unhappy about something, and, you know, put limits on misbehavior if it occurred.
sentences.zh: 给这些感受贴上标签，如果孩子对某事不高兴，帮助他们解决问题，并且，你知道，如果出现不当行为，要设定界限。

sentences.en: So those five steps of emotion coaching turned out to be really critical in the longitudinal development of emotional intelligence in their children.
sentences.zh: 所以，这五个情绪教练的步骤在孩子情商的纵向发展中被证明是非常关键的。

sentences.en: That was really kind of surprising.
sentences.zh: 这真的很令人惊讶。

sentences.en: So in fact, those parents were very different toward one another.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这些父母对彼此的态度也非常不同。

sentences.en: When one of them was emotional, the other parent would really zoom in and say, okay, baby, what are you feeling?
sentences.zh: 当其中一方情绪化时，另一方会真正关注并说，好吧，宝贝，你感觉如何？

sentences.en: Because when you're upset, the world stops and I listen.
sentences.zh: 因为当你难过时，世界就会停止，我会倾听。

sentences.en: And those were the emotion coaches.
sentences.zh: 这就是那些情绪教练。

sentences.en: So we really did discover that the way people interacted with one another was strongly related to the way they would zoom in on their child's emotions.
sentences.zh: 所以我们确实发现，人们相互互动的方式与他们关注孩子情绪的方式密切相关。

sentences.en: Well, and that had big implications for the longitudinal development of emotional intelligence in their child.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这对孩子情商的纵向发展有着巨大的影响。

sentences.en: So I think many of us have heard the advice that you shouldn't let the sun set on your anger.
sentences.zh: 所以我想我们很多人都听过这样的建议：不要带着愤怒过夜。

sentences.en: Don't go to bed mad.
sentences.zh: 不要带着气上床睡觉。

sentences.en: And I know you said that's a myth.
sentences.zh: 我知道你说过这是一个神话。

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 为什么这么说？

sentences.en: Because it's impossible to do.
sentences.zh: 因为这根本做不到。

sentences.en: Here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 问题在于。

sentences.en: There's a difference between wrath and anger, right?
sentences.zh: 愤怒（wrath）和生气（anger）是有区别的，对吧？

sentences.en: So, you know, the original statement really comes up in the Bible.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，最初的说法确实出自《圣经》。

sentences.en: But in the Bible, it's about wrath.
sentences.zh: 但在《圣经》中，它指的是愤怒（wrath）。

sentences.en: And wrath is, you know, the most severe, intense anger.
sentences.zh: 而愤怒（wrath）是，你知道，最严重、最强烈的愤怒。

sentences.en: It's rage, you know, multiplied a hundred times.
sentences.zh: 那是狂怒，你知道，放大了百倍。

sentences.en: So wrath also contains a lot of hatred, all kinds of stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以愤怒（wrath）也包含了很多仇恨，各种各样的东西。

sentences.en: So anger is hardwired in.
sentences.zh: 所以生气是与生俱来的。

sentences.en: You know, it's an emotion that is very primal to us.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一种对我们来说非常原始的情绪。

sentences.en: And if something has happened late at night that has really angered a partner, it's almost impossible for that person to then stop feeling
sentences.zh: 如果深夜发生了什么事让伴侣非常生气，那个人几乎不可能立刻停止感到

sentences.en: angry, feel loving and warm, go to bed and have sex.
sentences.zh: 生气，感到充满爱意和温暖，上床睡觉并发生性关系。

sentences.en: It's not going to happen usually.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下是不可能发生的。

sentences.en: I mean, maybe there are a few people out there that can do that, but most of us can't.
sentences.zh: 我是说，也许外面有少数人能做到，但我们大多数人做不到。

sentences.en: Makeup sex, yeah.
sentences.zh: 和好性爱，是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, makeup sex or just aggressive sex, you know, whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，和好性爱或者只是激烈的性爱，你知道，不管是什么。

sentences.en: Anyway,
sentences.zh: 总之，

sentences.en: so and couples who are successful couples don't follow that particular statement, you know, they don't do it.
sentences.zh: 所以，成功的夫妻并不遵循那种特定的说法，你知道，他们不会那样做。

sentences.en: So somebody may be angry and what they need to do is make sure that they're physiologically common enough to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 所以有人可能会生气，他们需要做的是确保自己在生理上足够平静，可以去睡觉。

sentences.en: They may still feel some anger, but they're not flooded.
sentences.zh: 他们可能仍然感到一些愤怒，但他们没有情绪过载。

sentences.en: Their heart rates are not 150 beats a minute.
sentences.zh: 他们的心率没有达到每分钟150次。

sentences.en: Otherwise, they'll never be able to sleep.
sentences.zh: 否则，他们永远无法入睡。

sentences.en: The mistake that couples make, here's the big one.
sentences.zh: 夫妻们犯的错误，这是最严重的一个。

sentences.en: And we can call this a myth.
sentences.zh: 我们可以称之为神话。

sentences.en: You're able to solve your problems late at night when you're tired.
sentences.zh: 你可以在深夜疲惫时解决问题。

sentences.en: No, you're not able to.
sentences.zh: 不，你做不到。

sentences.en: You can't do it.
sentences.zh: 你无法做到。

sentences.en: People are so tired by the ends of their days, right?
sentences.zh: 人们在一天结束时太累了，对吧？

sentences.en: Most of the time.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候。

sentences.en: They've worked hard or they have kids.
sentences.zh: 他们工作很辛苦，或者他们有孩子。

sentences.en: They've been raising their kids.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在抚养孩子。

sentences.en: Kids are running around like crazy.
sentences.zh: 孩子们像疯了一样跑来跑去。

sentences.en: So they're exhausted.
sentences.zh: 所以他们精疲力竭。

sentences.en: They're exhausted.
sentences.zh: 他们精疲力竭。

sentences.en: So to think that you can creatively problem solve or you can talk very gently and calmly and deeply late at night, there's your myth.
sentences.zh: 所以认为你可以在深夜创造性地解决问题，或者温和、冷静、深入地交谈，这就是你的神话。

sentences.en: And people should not try to do that.
sentences.zh: 人们不应该尝试那样做。

sentences.en: Thus, you know, the opposite is what people really, you know, might more realistically do, which is, yeah, you go to bed angry, but get a
sentences.zh: 因此，你知道，人们更现实的做法恰恰相反，那就是，是的，你可以带着愤怒上床，但要保证

sentences.en: good night's reSt. And the next day, then you talk about it when you're well rested and you actually have access to most of your mental powers.
sentences.zh: 充足的睡眠。第二天，当你休息好了，真正能够运用大部分智力时，再谈论它。

sentences.en: So just to wrap up, because this has been interesting and I could go on and on and on with, and I'm sure you could too, but we all have things to do.
sentences.zh: 所以总结一下，因为这次谈话很有趣，我可以一直说下去，我相信你也可以，但我们都有事情要做。

sentences.en: But I want to ask you this question.
sentences.zh: 但我还是想问你这个问题。

sentences.en: You have both been working in this space for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 你们俩在这个领域工作了很长时间。

sentences.en: Are there any big research questions on relationships that you feel you still need to answer?
sentences.zh: 关于关系，还有什么重大的研究问题是你觉得仍然需要回答的吗？

sentences.en: Let's both answer that.
sentences.zh: 我们俩都回答一下吧。

sentences.en: John, you want to start?
sentences.zh: 约翰，你想先开始吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: You know, the important thing to say is that all of these techniques, you know, like gentle
sentences.zh: 你知道，重要的一点是，所有这些技巧，比如温和的

sentences.en: startup, finding out the dreams within conflict, none of them work without trust and commitment being there in the relationship.
sentences.zh: 开场，找出冲突背后的梦想，如果没有信任和承诺，它们在关系中都无法奏效。

sentences.en: And trust means that people really are thinking for two.
sentences.zh: 信任意味着人们确实在为两个人着想。

sentences.en: They're thinking of the benefits of their partner.
sentences.zh: 他们在考虑伴侣的利益。

sentences.en: Conflict isn't a zero sum game.
sentences.zh: 冲突不是零和博弈。

sentences.en: One person wins and the other one loses, but they're really working collaboratively on the problem together.
sentences.zh: 不是一个人赢而另一个人输，而是他们真正地在共同协作解决问题。

sentences.en: And commitment really means that they've said, this is the journey of my life and nobody can replace you.
sentences.zh: 承诺确实意味着他们已经说过了，这是我生命中的旅程，没有人能取代你。

sentences.en: You know, there isn't, there isn't a woman on the planet that for me that can come close to Julie.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在这个星球上，对我来说，没有哪个女人能比得上朱莉。

sentences.en: She has my whole heart for my whole life and all of my money.
sentences.zh: 她拥有我的一生，我的整个心，以及我所有的钱。

sentences.en: And I have nothing to offer any other woman.
sentences.zh: 我对其他任何女人都没有什么可提供的。

sentences.en: Am I the luckiest woman on the planet?
sentences.zh: 我是这个星球上最幸运的女人吗？

sentences.en: So, you know, I mean, she's, she's really it for me.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我是说，她，她对我来说真的是唯一。

sentences.en: So, you know, Carol Rustbolt's research showed us how important commitment was.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，卡罗尔·拉斯特博尔特的研究向我们展示了承诺有多么重要。

sentences.en: And our research with the trust metric showed us how important that is.
sentences.zh: 我们的信任指标研究向我们展示了这一点有多重要。

sentences.en: Without trust and commitment, none of these techniques will work.
sentences.zh: 如果没有信任和承诺，这些技巧都不会奏效。

sentences.en: So we really don't understand what it is that goes into building trust and building commitment in some people and not others.
sentences.zh: 所以我们确实不明白，为什么有些人能建立信任和承诺，而有些人却不能。

sentences.en: It could be insecure attachment gets in the way, but we don't know the answer to that question.
sentences.zh: 这可能是因为不安全型依恋阻碍了这一过程，但我们还不知道这个问题的答案。

sentences.en: It's a really big research question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常重大的研究课题。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And here are mine.
sentences.zh: 这是我的观点。

sentences.en: So, so far, a couple of things we haven't had time to talk about, but one is that
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，还有几件事我们没时间讨论，但其中之一是

sentences.en: we have created a treatment, a particular treatment model that looks like it's really working to treat affairs, to treat betrayal.
sentences.zh: 我们已经创建了一种治疗方法，一种看起来在处理婚外情和背叛方面确实有效的特定治疗模型。

sentences.en: And we're very excited about that.
sentences.zh: 我们对此感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: We've done a, the first controlled randomized study of treatment, therapeutic treatment for affairs that's ever been done.
sentences.zh: 我们进行了有史以来第一次针对婚外情的治疗性干预的随机对照研究。

sentences.en: There haven't been any others done up until now.
sentences.zh: 在此之前还没有人做过类似的研究。

sentences.en: So we have pre and post, we're starting to get follow-up.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有治疗前后的数据，并且开始获得后续跟踪结果。

sentences.en: And our treatment looks very, very successful at this point.
sentences.zh: 目前看来，我们的治疗非常、非常成功。

sentences.en: We've also done a research study on the treatment of what's called situational domestic violence, which is minor to moderate domestic violence without a
sentences.zh: 我们还对所谓的“情境性家庭暴力”的治疗进行了一项研究，这指的是轻度到中度的家庭暴力，没有

sentences.en: clear perpetrator and a clear victim in which the victim can't do anything to change things.
sentences.zh: 明确的施暴者和受害者，受害者无法通过自身努力改变现状。

sentences.en: You know, the case being there where we've got to get the victim out of the relationship.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那种情况下我们必须让受害者脱离这段关系。

sentences.en: But with situational domestic violence, we actually do have a treatment that is very successful in eliminating domestic violence, eliminating hostility
sentences.zh: 但对于情境性家庭暴力，我们确实有一种治疗方法，在消除家庭暴力、消除伴侣间的敌意方面非常成功，

sentences.en: between the partners and increasing their friendship and connection.
sentences.zh: 并且能增进他们的友谊和联结。

sentences.en: But we still have to learn.
sentences.zh: 但我们仍需学习。

sentences.en: And this, of course, is one of my big thoughts about trying to help people.
sentences.zh: 当然，这也是我关于如何帮助人们的一个重要思考。

sentences.en: We need to help couples learn how to manage their relationships and strengthen their relationships when one or both partners has post-traumatic stress disorder.
sentences.zh: 我们需要帮助那些伴侣中有一方或双方患有创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）的夫妻，学习如何管理和加强他们的关系。

sentences.en: And these days, you know, between environmental calamities like Hurricane Helena and background abuse
sentences.zh: 如今，你知道，在像海伦娜飓风这样的环境灾难、成长背景中的虐待

sentences.en: and combat or, you know, shootings in schools, people are so traumatized they can't see straight.
sentences.zh: 以及战斗，或者学校枪击事件之间，人们受到的创伤太深，以至于无法理清思绪。

sentences.en: And oftentimes that stress will spill over into the relationship and contaminate the connection between the partners doctors.
sentences.zh: 这种压力往往会溢出到关系中，并污染伴侣之间的联结。

sentences.en: So I have started to create a treatment for couples where there is PTSD.
sentences.zh: 所以我已经开始为有PTSD的夫妻创建一种治疗方法。

sentences.en: But we haven't done a research study yet.
sentences.zh: 但我们还没有进行研究。

sentences.en: And I would really like to flesh out more that treatment model and test it with random controlled study.
sentences.zh: 我真的很想进一步完善那个治疗模型，并用随机对照研究来测试它。

sentences.zh: 好的，约翰，朱莉，非常感谢你们今天能来。

sentences.en: This has been really interesting.
sentences.zh: 这次谈话真的很有趣。

sentences.en: I think the work you do is so important and so helpful to many, many people.
sentences.zh: 我认为你们所做的工作非常重要，对许多许多人都有很大帮助。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.zh: 也谢谢你，金。

sentences.en: Wonderful interview.
sentences.zh: 很棒的采访。

sentences.zh: 但这真的很棒。
